runtime_gate.reason: Existing canonical F-host shared-runner heartbeat remains stale and height_difference_2 guarded operator recovery remains unexecuted.

score_basis: Non-statistical internal evidence-quality score based on current adopted London policy, current programme/monitoring pages and explicit separation of strategic targets, funding programmes, draft policy and scheme-specific viability evidence.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy H4
sources.fact: Adopted strategic target is 50% of new homes across London to be genuinely affordable; this is a London-wide target, not a parcel-specific affordable-housing requirement.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy H5
sources.fact: Threshold approach initially sets 35% affordable housing, or 50% for specified public/industrial land circumstances, subject to scheme type and Fast Track/Viability Tested Route criteria.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy H6
sources.fact: Policy sets affordable tenure split requirements; policy percentages are not a substitute for an application-specific tenure schedule or S106 agreement.

sources.label: London Plan 2021 Policy H7
sources.fact: Boroughs must monitor secured affordable housing and review mechanisms; monitoring does not prove delivery on a candidate parcel.

sources.label: Affordable Housing and Viability SPG
sources.fact: Explains the Threshold Approach and Fast Track Route; qualifying schemes must meet relevant affordable-housing and other policy requirements.

sources.label: London Social and Affordable Homes Programme 2026-36
sources.fact: Programme offers up to £11.7 billion and supports schemes capable of starting by March 2036 and completing by March 2039; programme availability is not a site funding award.

sources.label: London Assembly Affordable Housing Monitor 2026
sources.fact: Published 8 July 2026; reports 14,335 affordable housing starts under AHP 2021-26 by March 2026 against a revised 17,800-19,000 target range. Programme performance is not parcel delivery probability.

sources.label: LBBD Housing Strategy 2026-31 consultation
sources.fact: Council page says consultation has concluded and affordability was a major issue; consultation evidence is not treated as an adopted planning policy or scheme consent.

sources.label: LBBD Local Plan 2037
sources.fact: Adopted 18 September 2024 and remains part of the current development-plan evidence; application-specific affordable housing requirements still need exact policy/site binding.

sources.label: LBBD Developer contributions
sources.fact: Section 106 can secure affordable housing and mitigation; generic S106 policy does not prove the amount or tenure secured for an unverified parcel.

sources.label: Draft London Plan 2026 homes chapter
sources.fact: Published 16 July 2026 with publication status Draft; emerging HN policies are not substituted for adopted London Plan 2021 policy during consultation.

sources.label: Current London Plan status
sources.fact: London Plan 2021 remains the current adopted planning framework while work proceeds on the next London Plan.

examples.result: London-wide H4 50% target is not assigned as a parcel-specific affordable percentage.
H5 35%/50% thresholds require scheme classification and policy criteria; no threshold is applied without an actual proposal.
H6 tenure split is policy context and not a substitute for a secured application/S106 tenure schedule.
LSAHP up-to-£11.7bn programme availability is not treated as a funding award to any candidate site.
AHP 2021-26 delivery-monitor figures are programme-level monitoring and not parcel-level delivery probability.
LBBD Housing Strategy 2026-31 consultation is not silently treated as adopted planning policy.
Draft London Plan 2026 HN policies remain explicitly DRAFT and do not replace adopted 2021 policies.
No viability/affordable-housing promotion occurs without exact scheme, tenure, policy, S106 and viability evidence where applicable.
